In Intermittently dried desert channels with moderate runoff, a dried river bed is transformed into an Intermmittent Dammed channel through barcan formation and damming by eolian dunes. In High-stability desert channels with high runoff, a river channel is transformed into a No dammed-channel pattern through vegetation.

During storms, Beach Berm sand is transformed into Offshore sandbars through transport by Wave action and deposition. During calm weather, offshore sand is moved onto the beach and stored as Beach Berms through transport by Swell waves. River sediment is transformed into Coastal dunes through transport and deposition during Flash Flood events.

During stage (b), former channel sediment is transformed into a deeper channel through debris-flow-induced erosion along the section boundary. During stage (c), former channel sediment is transformed into remnant deposits through continued debris-flow erosion and deposition.

During stage 2 ice-margin recession from LF 3 to LF 4, former valley floor deposits are transformed into an ice berg through iceberg calving. During stage 3 ice-margin recession from LF 4 to LF 5, the ice berg is transformed into a delta foreset through submarine deposition. During stage 4 ice-margin advance during the Glaciotectonic event, subglacial mass flow is transformed into thrust stacks through thrust faulting. During stage 5 ice-margin recession from LF 5 to LF 6, thrust stacks are transformed into relict knickpoints through erosion.

During stage I Initial phase, a Rockslide body is transformed into partially ice-filled joints through percolating-heaving. During stage II Percolating-heaving, frost heave by ice segregation develops along the partially ice-filled joints. During stage III Enhanced percolating-heaving, a Rock mass containing a Reserved ice block is transformed into a Rock/ice block through sliding.

During stage (b), saprolite is transformed into pisoliths through weathering without pedoturbation under stable conditions. During stage (c), transported pisoliths are transformed into calcrete through deposition during increased aridity. During stage (d), the calcrete sequence is transformed into relict colluvium through valley incision by creeks and rivers.

During the D1 phase, the Corte Slices are transformed into a deeper buried tectonic wedge through Underthrusting within the European continental crust. During the D2 phase, the tectonic wedge is transformed into exhumed continental crust through continuous exhumation without faulting. During the D3 phase, the same continental crust is transformed into more deeply exhumed continental crust containing a low-angle normal fault through extensional tectonics.
